beats.text: What if one server can't handle all your users?
beats.say: What happens when one server can't handle all your users?

beats.text: One server = one limit, and one failure takes everything down.
beats.say: With a single server, you have one limit, and one failure takes everything down.

beats.text: A load balancer spreads traffic across many servers.
beats.say: A load balancer sits in front and spreads the traffic across many servers.

beats.text: Round robin: A, B, C, then start over.
beats.say: The simplest strategy is round robin. Request one goes to server A, two to B, three to C, then it starts over.

beats.text: Least connections: busy servers get a break.
beats.say: Smarter balancers send each request to the server with the fewest active connections, so busy servers get a break.

beats.text: Health checks: dead servers get no traffic.
beats.say: And if a server dies, health checks notice, and the load balancer stops sending it traffic.
